Title: Geschichtschreiber der husitischen Bewegung in Böhmen, herausgegeben von Dr. K. Höfler. Theil I (Fontes rerum Austriacarum, Scriptores II)
Creator: Constantin von Höfler (1811-1897), editor; the contributions are Latin and Czech chronicles, tracts and proceedings of the Hussite period.
Publisher: Wien: aus der k. k. Hof- und Staatsdruckerei (Fontes rerum Austriacarum, Erste Abtheilung, Scriptores, II. Band)
Publication Date: 1856
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads '1856' (read in the OCR); the Internet Archive item record carries the Public Domain Mark 1.0 licence (creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/).
Language: lat (mixed: Latin chronicles and documents with Höfler's German introduction and notes)
Source: Internet Archive item bub_gb_3fyRbn_1No4C (archive.org/details/bub_gb_3fyRbn_1No4C), full-text file bub_gb_3fyRbn_1No4C_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows unchanged apart from this header. Nothing stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. Sampled at opening, middle and end: the first pages are stamp and noise; the body Latin is readable with scattered letter errors.
Content note: Höfler's first volume of Hussite sources: the Trebon chronicle, Procopius the notary, the old collegiate chronicle of Prague, the proceedings and articles around Hus at Constance, and the 'Articuli sacerdotum hereticorum et Pikharditarum' with the absolution that follows (the Picard articles, on a radical group in the Taborite orbit; whether the Picards and the Adamites are one sect is left to the build), and the 'Anonymus de origine Taboritarum et de morte Wenceslai IV'. Mixed voices: Prague chroniclers, Hus's accusers and the proceedings against the Picards. The Picard articles are a hostile record of a radical group, written by its opponents.
